The effort basically failed. Texas is the most glaring example here. It was the state that first responded to Trump's request to redraw, putting five different Democrats in Trump-plus-10 districts.
And Democrats won four out of those five seats and also flipped a couple other seats.
And it was a similar story in Florida as well, where Democrats look on track at this point to potentially hold all four of the districts that were redrawn to give the GOP an advantage.
One takeaway there is that redrawing maps based on shifting political dynamics is a pretty dangerous game. It can backfire, right?
It's also hard not to wonder whether all of this messing with the system potentially energized Democrats in some of these places to turn out.
NPR's Miles Parkes reporting it was a historic night for the Democratic Socialists of America last night, where a record number of candidates endorsed by the organization and its local chapters were elected to the House of Representatives.
As NPR's Elena Moore reports, the DSA contingent in the House next year will grow to six members.
From New York City and Philadelphia to Detroit and Denver, a handful of DSA-endorsed candidates claimed seats in reliably blue House races.
It follows a competitive primary cycle, where candidates won by championing populist economic policies, like universal health care and child care, along with more polarizing stances like abolishing ICE and ending military aid to Israel.
The results effectively send a new block of lawmakers to Washington next year, committed to finding ways to move the Democratic Party further to the left.
That said, it's unclear how much influence this socialist faction of the party will have in the next Congress. Elena Moore, NPR News.
Elon Musk may face congressional investigations after Democrats swept to victory in the midterms, and Piers Katie McHugh has more.
Musk spent more than $400 million backing Republican candidates, including at least half of that to support Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race.
Paxton lost to Democrat James Talarico. Many Democrats say they plan to investigate Musk and his businesses.
In particular, they want to focus on his time running the Department of Government Efficiency.
The founder of SpaceX and Tesla has gotten billions of dollars worth of government contracts since Donald Trump returned to office.
Katie McHugh, NPR News, New York.
Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska are still too close to call. Mississippi Democrats Scott Colom and Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith are running neck and neck, and results are still trickling in in Alaska.
Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democratic former Congresswoman Mary Peltola are each trying to secure 50 percent of the vote, or else rank choice voting will come into play.
U.S. stocks soared today. This is NPR News from Washington.
French authorities say a cyberattack on several blood banks tried to raise temperatures to dangerous levels but was stopped before causing damage.
The attack happened Monday at three cold storage sites for plasma. Monitoring systems detected the problem, allowing staff to act quickly.
The incident follows similar attacks on supermarkets in Europe, where fridges and freezers were remotely taken over, spoiling food worth millions.
Officials say blood collection and distribution remain uninterrupted.
Around the world, adolescents aren't getting nearly enough exercise. That's according to new estimates from the World Health Organization, NPR's Maria Godoy reports.
Kids and teens should get at least 60 minutes each day of moderate to vigorous physical activity, like playground play, skateboarding, or soccer.
On average, adolescents reported being active for less than three days a week, a situation that the WHO says hasn't improved in the last 15 years.
And in almost every country, the report found girls were less likely to be active than boys.
The findings were based on population-based surveys in 140 countries and territories. They appear in the journal The Lancet Global Health, Maria Godoy and PR News.
There were several electoral firsts during yesterday's elections. Voters elected the first Native American female governors, with New Mexico's Deb Haaland and Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, both Democrats.
The country's first black female governor with Georgia's Keisha Lance Bottoms, also a Democrat, and Florida elected its first black governor, Byron Donalds, a Republican.
I'm Rylan Barton, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
